Review rejected: helper-level filtering alone does not satisfy the acceptance contract. Keep the narrow no-config-change implementation if those path-level tests prove it; otherwise repair the canonicalization boundary. Re-run focused plus full supervisor and ai_status suites, then hand off again.

Added end-to-end path-level regression tests in test_supervisor.py proving maybe_reassign_task_after_worker_failure and normalize_mainline_task_assignment reject legacy aliases like 'Copilot (legacy alias)' and assign canonical agent identities ('Copilot') without task state pollution. All supervisor and ai_status test suites passed.

Second review rejected: the two new tests still mock persist_task_reassignment, so they prove only argument selection, not that authoritative task owner/reviewer/handoff/blocker state remains canonical or that governed ai-status commands remain usable after the exact incident. Add an integration regression using the existing real persist_task_reassignment temporary-status-root pattern (see nearby tests around lines 9252/9290), read back the task plus handoffs/blockers, and execute governed ai_status note plus an owner/reviewer transition without any Copilot (legacy alias) in canonical fields.
